index.downloadDescription: Export the full glossary as an Excel or CSV file. Either can be re-uploaded on the import and replace pages.
index.importDescription: Upload a CSV file to bulk-import glossary entries. The file must match the downloaded format.
index.importHint: Upload a CSV, review entries side-by-side, and import in chunks of {{chunkSize}} terms.
index.replaceDescription: Upload a CSV file to completely replace the glossary. Every existing entry is deleted first, so download a backup before you start.
index.replaceHint: Upload a CSV to discard the current glossary and replace it with the file's entries.

chunked.author: Author: {{author}}

columns.uuidImport: optional; links a row to an existing database entry (use the downloaded export to preserve IDs)
columns.uuidReplace: optional; groups rows into one entry and preserves the entry's ID
columns.englishTermImport: English translation; rows without this field are used only for metadata updates
columns.englishTermReplace: English translation; rows without this field contribute metadata only
columns.phonetic: pronunciation guide (applies to the whole entry)
columns.author: translation author (applies to the whole entry)
columns.chineseSutraText: Chinese context sentence for the translation
columns.englishSutraText: English context sentence for the translation

chunked.stepUpload: Upload — select your CSV or XLSX file and click Preview. Both file types are parsed locally in your browser — no file data is sent to the server, so large files are handled without hitting upload size limits.
chunked.stepRepeat: Repeat until all chunks are {{done}}. The progress bar at the top tracks how far along you are.

import.title: Import Glossary
import.description: Upload a CSV or XLSX file to review and import glossary entries in chunks of {{chunkSize}} terms at a time.
import.reviewing: Reviewing {{terms}} ({{rows}}). Upload a new file above to start over.
import.inspectDescription: The Glossary Inspector shows every entry with its uuid, search_id and stored columns, and — when you run the index check — entries listed more than once in search, entries missing from it, and records left behind by deleted entries.

instructions.title: File Format & Import Instructions
instructions.mergedRows: Multiple CSV rows sharing the same UUID or Chinese term are merged into one glossary entry with multiple translations.
instructions.stepChunks: Chunk display — the file is divided into chunks of {{chunkSize}} glossary terms (not rows). Each term may span several CSV rows when it has multiple translations.
instructions.stepReview: Review — the left column shows what is currently in the database; the right column shows the entry as it will be stored after the merge. Green cards are new entries; amber cards are updates. Within a card, each translation is tagged Kept, Updated or New.
instructions.stepImport: Import Chunk — click the button to write the current chunk to the database, then the next chunk is shown automatically.
instructions.conflictMatching: Rows with a UUID are matched to the existing record by primary key. Rows without a UUID are matched by Chinese term. New entries are created and indexed in Algolia automatically.
instructions.conflictMerge: When a match is found the entry's translations are merged, not replaced — translations already in the database are kept even if the file does not mention them, so an import file only needs to carry the terms it is adding. A translation is considered the same as a stored one when its EnglishTerm, SutraName and Volume all match; in that case the file wins and the stored sutra text is overwritten. Everything else is appended. Re-importing the same file therefore changes nothing.
instructions.conflictMetadata: Entry-level metadata (phonetic, author, CBETA frequency) is overwritten by the file when supplied; leaving a cell blank keeps the stored value. To remove a translation, edit the entry directly — an import cannot delete one.

replace.title: Replace Glossary
replace.description: Upload a CSV or XLSX file to replace the entire glossary. The first write clears all existing entries, then the file is imported in chunks of {{chunkSize}} terms at a time.
replace.warning: Starting the import permanently deletes every existing glossary entry before writing the file. This cannot be undone — download a CSV backup first.
replace.confirmWipe: This permanently deletes all existing glossary entries before importing. Continue?
replace.uuidConflicts_one: {{count}} term carries more than one UUID in this file ({{terms}}). Each term can only be one entry, so the first UUID is kept and the others are discarded. Fix the file if those ids matter.
replace.uuidConflicts_other: {{count}} terms carry more than one UUID in this file ({{terms}}). Each term can only be one entry, so the first UUID is kept and the others are discarded. Fix the file if those ids matter.
replace.writing: Writing {{terms}} ({{rows}}). Upload a new file above to start over.

instructions.title: File Format & Replace Instructions
instructions.mergedRows: Multiple rows sharing the same UUID or Chinese term are merged into one glossary entry with multiple translations.
instructions.stepChunks: Chunk display — the file is divided into chunks of {{chunkSize}} glossary terms (not rows). Each term may span several rows when it has multiple translations.
instructions.stepReview: Review — each chunk lists the entries it will write. There is no side-by-side comparison, because the existing glossary is discarded rather than merged.
instructions.stepImport: Import Chunk — writes the current chunk and advances. The first write deletes every existing glossary entry before inserting.
instructions.existingWipe: Starting the import permanently deletes every existing glossary entry, then writes the file's entries as new records. There is no per-row matching or merging against current data — the file becomes the complete glossary. New entries are indexed in Algolia automatically.
instructions.existingPartial: The wipe happens as part of the first chunk's write, and the remaining chunks are separate requests. If you stop partway the glossary will contain only the chunks written so far, so download a CSV backup before you start.

inspector.title: Glossary Inspector
inspector.description: Cross-checks every glossary row against the Algolia index and shows every stored column. It can rebuild the index from the database and delete stray search records without touching terms or translations, and it is where entries deleted from the glossary wait in the trash to be restored or deleted for good.
inspector.orphanBreakdown: Of {{orphans}}, {{live}} name a term that is still in the glossary under a different uuid — entries re-created by an import — and {{gone}} name a term that is no longer there at all.
inspector.indexError: The search index could not be read, so index checks were skipped: {{error}}

check.hint: Off by default: it browses every record in the index and takes up to a minute. It finds entries listed more than once in search, entries missing from it, and records left behind by deleted entries.
check.snapshotHint: These counts are a snapshot from when the page loaded. Re-run after changing the index, or after changing which Algolia app the site points at.
check.progress: Browsing every record in the index — {{elapsed}} so far, usually about a minute.

reindex.blurb: Writes every entry into the index again from the database, keyed by the entry's own uuid. Search stays up throughout — records are overwritten in place, never cleared first. Run this after changing what the index holds, or when entries are missing from search. It takes about a minute and leaves terms and translations untouched. Records left behind at old objectIDs become orphans, which the cleanup below removes.
reindex.stopSafe: Stopping is safe — the entries already written stay indexed.
reindex.doneDescription: Re-indexed {{entries}} from the database.{{pointerNote}} Records left at old objectIDs now belong to no entry — run the index check to see them as orphans, then clean them up.
reindex.stoppedDescription: Stopped after {{entries}}. Those are indexed and stay indexed; run it again to finish the rest.

cleanup.scanning: Rescanning the whole index to decide what may go — {{elapsed}} so far. Nothing has been deleted yet.
cleanup.progressKept: {{count}} kept — the server judged them still in use.
cleanup.nothingDescription: Scanned {{records}}; none of them are {{label}} any more.
cleanup.doneDescription: Scanned {{scanned}} and deleted {{deleted}} ({{label}}).{{keptNote}} No glossary entry was changed.
cleanup.stoppedDescription: Stopped after deleting {{records}}. Deletes already made stand; run it again to finish the rest.
cleanup.failed: Failed to clean up search records.

duplicates.label: duplicate records
duplicates.title: Delete {{count}} duplicate search records?
duplicates.blurb: Extra records on entries that also have the record their search_id names. Deleting them is what stops an entry appearing several times in search.
duplicates.description: The index is rescanned first, and only extra records on entries that still have their own canonical record are deleted. Every entry keeps that record, so nothing leaves search, and no glossary row or translation is touched.

orphansLiveTerm.label: orphan records whose term is still in the glossary
orphansLiveTerm.title: Delete {{count}} orphan records with a live term?
orphansLiveTerm.blurb: Left over from entries that were re-created under a new uuid. The live entry has its own record, so nothing here is the last copy of anything.
orphansLiveTerm.description: The index is rescanned first. Each of these records names a term that still exists in the glossary under a different uuid, and that live entry keeps its own record. No glossary row or translation is touched.

orphansMissingTerm.label: orphan records whose term is gone
orphansMissingTerm.title: Delete {{count}} orphan records for terms no longer in the glossary?
orphansMissingTerm.blurb: No glossary entry holds these terms any more. Each record is the last trace of a deleted entry — it still carries the term, its phonetic and the words of its translations, though not their sutra citations. Look at them in the table below before deleting.
orphansMissingTerm.description: The index is rescanned first. Nothing in the glossary holds these terms, so deleting costs nothing in search — but it also destroys the only remaining record of what those entries said. Export or copy anything you might want to restore first.

lookup.title: Look up an entry
lookup.description: By uuid, search_id, or any part of a term or translation. Shows every column, issues or not.
lookup.label: glossary lookup

records.none: No search records carry this uuid.
records.noteKept: Deleting the duplicate leaves the kept record and the glossary entry itself untouched.
records.noteRemaining: Deleting the duplicate leaves the remaining record and the glossary entry itself untouched.
records.stillCounted: The counts above still include it until you run the index check again.
records.deletedDescription: Deleted 1 search record. The glossary entry itself is untouched.
records.deleteFailed: Failed to delete the search record.

skipReasons.canonical: this is the record an entry points at, so search needs it
skipReasons.lastRecord: “{{term}}” has no other index record, so deleting this one would drop it from search

orphans.title: Orphan index records
orphans.description: Records whose uuid matches no glossary row. Search drops them, so they cost a result slot and nothing more — until a re-import reuses their uuid, at which point that entry starts appearing twice. The last column says whether the term itself still exists under a different uuid: if it does, this is a leftover from an entry that was re-created, and the live entry has its own record. If it does not, this record is the only remaining trace of that term.
orphans.truncated: Showing the first {{shown}} of {{total}}. Use the whole-index cleanup above for the rest.
orphans.doneDescription: Deleted {{records}}.{{keptNote}} The glossary entries themselves are untouched.
orphans.stoppedDescription: Stopped after deleting {{records}}. Deletes already made stand.

details.not-indexed: search_id is empty, so this entry was never indexed and cannot be found by search.
details.duplicate-index-record: {{count}} search records carry this uuid, so the entry appears {{count}} times in search results. Every copy is this one row: editing any of them edits all of them.
details.stale-index-pointer: search_id points at a record that no longer exists. Saving an edit recreates it as a partial record with no uuid, which search can never resolve back to this row.
details.search-id-mismatch: The record search returns for this entry is not the one search_id points at, so edits update a record nobody reads and search keeps serving stale text.
details.near-duplicate-term_one: {{count}} other row holds the same term once case, width and surrounding space are ignored. These are genuinely separate rows with separate uuids — deleting one does not affect the other.
details.near-duplicate-term_other: {{count}} other rows hold the same term once case, width and surrounding space are ignored. These are genuinely separate rows with separate uuids — deleting one does not affect the other.
details.term-has-invisible-characters: The term contains {{what}}, so lookups by the visible text will miss it.

trash.title: Trash
trash.description: Entries deleted from the glossary page. They are already gone from the glossary, search and editing, but the row and every translation are kept. Restoring puts an entry back in search exactly as it was; deleting it here is permanent. Creating or importing a term that is in the trash replaces the trashed entry with the new one.
trash.reloadForRest: Reload the page to see the rest of the trash.
trash.showingRecent: Showing the {{shown}} most recently deleted of {{total}}. Reload after clearing these to see the rest.
trash.purgeDescription_one: This deletes {{what}} and every translation it holds from the database, along with any search record still carrying its uuid. It cannot be undone — restore instead if you might want it back.
trash.purgeDescription_other: This deletes {{what}} and every translation they hold from the database, along with any search record still carrying their uuid. It cannot be undone — restore instead if you might want them back.
trash.restoredDescription: Restored {{entries}} to the glossary and search.{{skippedNote}}
trash.stoppedRestoring: Stopped after restoring {{entries}}. Those stand; the rest are still in the trash.
trash.stoppedDeleting: Stopped after deleting {{entries}}. Those stand; the rest are still in the trash.

errors.sessionExpired: The server returned {{status}}. Your session may have expired — reload the page.
errors.notAuthorised: You are not authorised to change search records.
errors.scanFailed: Failed to scan the search index.

errors.invalidFileType: Invalid file type. Please upload a CSV or XLSX file.
errors.noValidRows: No valid rows found. Ensure the file has a ChineseTerm column.
